title: Redwood Edgecases Demo: Long Context + High TPS Streaming Backpressure/Timeouts
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked AtlasPay through an edge-cases focused demo covering very long context windows, a high TPS traffic profile, streaming response backpressure behavior, and timeout/fallback policies. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for payments data residency; main concerns are latency tail, deterministic SLAs, and integration with their KMS. Action: provide pricing, run a benchmark with AtlasPay payloads, share SOC2/security pack, schedule POC kickoff.

Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (AtlasPay VP Eng), Anika Patel (CTO), Liam O'Neill (Platform), Sofia Ramos (Security)

Auto Summary: Walkthrough focused on edge-case scenarios: very long contexts, high concurrent TPS, streaming backpressure and timeouts; discussed Dedicated/Private options and security/compliance needs. Agreed next steps: benchmarks, payload samples, pricing and SOC2 pack.

[00:00] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone thanks for joining uh today we're gonna run through a very scoped demo - edge cases - long context and high TPS and streaming backpressure, um Priya's gonna drive the technical part.
[00:18] Marcus Li: Thanks Jordan, we really want to see how Redwood behaves when we hit 30k-40k token contexts and when our router floods at peak - roughly 2k rps at the front doors during batch jobs.
[00:32] Priya Nambiar: cool, yeah so we'll start with a quick architecture overview then jump to a live demo. note: I'm using the Redwood Console and the API in parallel.
[00:44] Anika Patel: quick ask - data residency and KMS before we start - we can't have any PII leave our VPC for the POC unless it's encrypted with our HSM key.
[00:55] Jordan Blake: totally, we'll cover Private and Dedicated options and KMS integrations, um we'll also attach the SOC2 pack after the call.
[01:12] Priya Nambiar: architecture slide: Redwood serving runtime with KV cache, continuous batching, and smart routing. apologies my slide says "KV cash" - transcription/typo, but it's KV cache.
[01:30] Liam O'Neill: can you explain how continuous batching interacts with low-latency singletons? our latency SLOs for auth flows are 100 ms.
[01:44] Priya Nambiar: yes so we have a latency tiering policy, requests flagged as latency-sensitive can bypass batching or get dispatched to lower batch sizes; also we do prefix caching for repeated prompts - that reduces effective tokens.
[02:05] Marcus Li: what about streaming? if a client disconnects or is slow, how does Redwood handle backpressure? we saw a lot of timeouts in our internal tests with other providers.
[02:18] Priya Nambiar: great question - streaming is multi-path: we stream tokens as they are generated, but we have server-side buffering and backpressure signals; if the client is slow we can pause generator threads and evict buffers based on policy, and there's a configurable client timeout plus automatic fallback to synchronous non-streaming call to finish a generation. note: sometimes the logging will show "back presure" spelled weird in older builds.
[02:45] Anika Patel: the fallback to a different model variant - does that change tokenization or output shape? we have strict parsers.
[02:57] Priya Nambiar: we try to preserve output shape via schema enforcement and function-calling; model variants are selected for compatibility (ie same tokenizer family). in practice we keep the same decoding settings.
[03:20] Jordan Blake: ok demo time - Priya will open console and we'll hit a long-context example.
[03:30] Priya Nambiar: starting long-context test: uploading a 42k-token document and asking a multi-part question that references earlier sections. invoking via Redwood API with ?stream=true to show streaming.
[04:00] Speaker 6: um can you repeat the prompt?
[04:06] Priya Nambiar: sure - prompt: "Summarize the risk sections and produce a remediation plan referencing section ids 2, 14, and 88" - then we append a 42k token history.
[04:20] [04:20] Transcript noise - network hiccup, small stutter
[04:33] Priya Nambiar: starting generation - streaming tokens incoming... first 2k tokens arrive in ~1.2s then steady stream. we show the console token timeline - notice the KV cache hit for repeated references.
[05:02] Marcus Li: hmm it's fast but will this hold under high TPS?
[05:08] Priya Nambiar: we'll simulate a concurrent load next - but for long context it's mostly memory/kv and seq-len execution path; we do chunked attention and memory paging for >context window models.
[05:30] Jordan Blake: quick note: for very long contexts we recommend model quantization profiles and a Dedicated pool so you get deterministic tail latencies.
[05:48] Liam O'Neill: what GPU types are you using in Dedicated? A100? H100? cost tradeoffs?
[05:56] Priya Nambiar: Dedicated can run on H100, A100 or mixed fleets; kernel selection happens at compile-time based on sequence length distribution; we typically recommend H100 for long-context/higher throughput but quantify cost in our Optimize recommendations.
[06:20] Priya Nambiar: ok now switching to synthetic high-TPS test. I'm running our test harness that replays AtlasPay traffic at 2k rps, with 50% requests being short (50 tokens) and 10% being long (10k tokens).
[06:40] [06:40] harness logs: spawning 2000 virtual clients
[06:45] Priya Nambiar: streaming enabled; we're measuring 95th and 99th percentiles and token/sec. first minute results coming in...
[07:10] Priya Nambiar: early signal: 95th latency for short requests ~120 ms on hosted, bursts cause queuing - we show the Console per-route latency heatmap.
[07:28] Marcus Li: 120 ms is above our 100 ms SLO for auth - you said latency tiering - can we guarantee bypass for those flags?
[07:38] Priya Nambiar: yes we can bind priority tags and route those to pre-warmed low-batch capacity nodes; with Dedicated you can reserve capacity to avoid queuing.
[07:55] Anika Patel: what happens when the streaming buffers fill during high concurrency? do you drop connections?
[08:04] Priya Nambiar: we have configurable eviction and backpressure policies; default is to signal the client to apply backpressure, then if the client doesn't keep up we can convert the stream to a background sync request and deliver result via a callback/webhook. we do not silently drop without logging.
[08:25] Sofia Ramos: logging and audit - will I get a full tamper-evident audit trail for each request including model variant and kernel choices?
[08:33] Jordan Blake: yes, audit logs include model/version, routing decision, kernel profile, latency buckets and KMS key ids if encryption used - we can expose via the Console and send to your SIEM.
[08:50] Priya Nambiar: now we're going to inject client slowdowns to observe timeouts. switching to test scenario: keep 5% of clients at 50ms network, 5% with 2s stall.
[09:12] [09:12] streaming trace: stalled clients show paused token emission; we trigger fallback after configured client-timeout 1.5s and convert to sync for those requests - you can see the event in the trace as "stream->sync-fallback".
[09:40] Marcus Li: interesting, so we'll still get final output even if the client stalls? what's the latency delta?
[09:48] Priya Nambiar: fallback adds some overhead - typically an extra 200-400 ms, depends on token count; for long-context it's higher because of rehydrating generator state.
[10:05] Liam O'Neill: for rehydration are you storing KV cache on disk or remote? disk across nodes? curious about egress and cross-AZ cost.
[10:15] Priya Nambiar: KV cache is memory-first, with spill-to-disk for older entries; in Dedicated we colocate storage so cross-AZ is avoided; for Private deployments you control network topology and costs.
[10:40] Jordan Blake: quick objection we often hear - "that's complicated, I'd rather just use OpenAI" - how do you position versus them?
[10:51] Priya Nambiar: we position as production-first with deterministic controls: batching, routing, fallbacks, and observability - other providers may be simpler but less predictable at scale.
[11:10] Anika Patel: security: can you bring your own HSM? our compliance requires customer-controlled key material.
[11:20] Jordan Blake: yes, BYOK via customer-managed KMS and HSM is supported in Private and Dedicated with a control-plane integration; we'll include the KMS integration guide.
[11:36] [11:36] minor audio overlap, two people talk at once
[11:45] Priya Nambiar: demo continues - now a scenario with pathological tokenization - we send adversarial payloads with lots of unicode. streaming keeps pace but we show some mis-tokenizations in one model variant; we then failover to a variant with a different tokenizer family which preserves schema.
[12:12] Marcus Li: ok if variant switch occurs, do you preserve conversation ids for downstream services? we need idempotency.
[12:22] Priya Nambiar: yes conversation id is preserved; routing layer records the switch and the Console shows a "fallback" badge.
[12:40] Jordan Blake: we usually recommend testing with your real payloads - that way Optimize can recommend quantization and kernel configs.
[12:52] Marcus Li: we'll share a sample of 1k real requests and the size distribution.
[13:00] Priya Nambiar: perfect, please include the worst-case long ones.
[13:06] [13:06] console: opening Optimize tab - shows recommended batching, quant profiles, and expected cost savings for this traffic profile (we show ~37% token-cost reduction with caching + quantization recommendations).
[13:35] Anika Patel: does Optimize include expected latency impact? we can't trade too much latency for cost.
[13:43] Priya Nambiar: yes Optimize shows latency vs cost curves and suggests pins for Reserved Dedicated pools if you need tighter tails.
[14:05] Priya Nambiar: now showing error mode: simulate timeouts - we set client timeout to 800ms and flood with long requests - see timeout counts rise and automatic fallback kicks in to a lower-cost model to finish generation or we return partials per policy.
[14:35] Liam O'Neill: partials might break our parsers - can we force atomic responses?
[14:44] Priya Nambiar: you can set atomic=true on the API which will withhold partials and either complete or return an error - it's a tradeoff.
[14:58] Marcus Li: if we use atomic=true and a timeout happens, do you retry? we want to avoid duplicates for side-effecting ops.
[15:08] Priya Nambiar: our default is no automatic retry for atomic requests; you can configure idempotency keys and the client can re-open a request, or the platform can write result to a webhook once available.
[15:30] Jordan Blake: higher level commercial q: pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted for this use-case?
[15:38] Jordan Blake: hosted pricing is usage-based; Dedicated is a reserved capacity model with monthly commit. I'll send a dedicated playbook with numbers.
[15:52] Marcus Li: procurement will need an enterprise agreement, and we need SLAs for 99.95% and P95 latency goals.
[16:03] Jordan Blake: noted - we have SLA tiers and enterprise legal templates; we'll loop in legal if you want.
[16:18] [16:18] small pause, screen share swapped to logs view
[16:25] Priya Nambiar: now live-dashboard under high load - you can see per-route token/sec, per-node latency histograms and backpressure events.
[16:50] Sofia Ramos: regarding audit logs: will logs contain full request body? that's sensitive.
[16:58] Jordan Blake: by default we redact PII, but for Private/Dedicated you can opt in to full logs stored in your environment and integrate with your SIEM.
[17:15] Marcus Li: for the POC we'd prefer Dedicated in our VPC, but we need to validate throughput numbers first.
[17:25] Priya Nambiar: understood - we'll run benchmarks with your payloads and simulate your 2k rps burst profile.
[17:38] [17:38] test - 2k rps sustained for 5 minutes - console shows CPU/GPU saturation then graceful fallback to queued nodes
[17:55] Priya Nambiar: during burst we saw queueing on hosted; Dedicated with reserved nodes eliminated queuing in this run.
[18:10] Liam O'Neill: any concerns about cold-starts for model variants during traffic spikes?
[18:18] Priya Nambiar: we recommend pre-warming model shards; for Dedicated we provide pre-warm policy; on hosted we have autoscaler but cold-start can add 200-500 ms for large models.
[18:40] Marcus Li: can you show the trace for a failed connection with backpressure?
[18:47] Priya Nambiar: pulling trace: here's a request that hit backpressure, we signaled client, then converted to sync; event stream shows 'signal->pause->sync-fallback' and an associated audit log entry.
[19:10] Marcus Li: good. question around data residency - for Dedicated in our VPC, is control plane still with Redwood? how much metadata crosses our network?
[19:22] Jordan Blake: control plane remains with Redwood for hosted; for Private you can run control plane in your cloud; for Dedicated we can offer a hybrid: customer-managed networking + pegged egress policies. metadata minimal but we can do an architecture review.
[19:45] Anika Patel: timeline - if we sign a POC, how long until we can test in prod-like environment?
[19:53] Jordan Blake: POC typically 2-4 weeks to run benchmarks and integrate SDKs; Dedicated provisioning takes longer (lead time for GPU capacity) - we can scope fast-path for evaluation in ~2 weeks if you accept shared hosted infra with reserved capacity.
[20:15] [20:15] minor transcript artifact - "uhm" repeated
